notes: New: find an address. Click the magnifying glass at the top right (it takes no room on the map until you do), type an address, a town or a place and press Enter: the map goes there and puts a pin on it, ready to plan a flight

With Azure Maps, Azure's addresses, Azure's places and OpenStreetMap are all asked and listed together, best match first (roads last unless you search for a road). With the other maps, the addresses come from OpenStreetMap
Can't find a spot by name? Paste its coordinates (in Google Maps: right-click the spot and click the numbers at the top) and the map goes straight there
New: right-click the map (or press and hold on a phone) and choose "Create a flight plan here": a new plan starts with its take-off point on that spot. With a plan open, the same menu adds a waypoint
New: in the Plans tab, a purple flag on the map shows where each saved plan takes off. Point at one for its name, click it to open the plan

The flight planner is less crowded on a computer: what you change (name, Save, waypoints, When, Notes) is in the left sidebar while a plan is open, and a short strip at the bottom shows the distance, time, battery, warnings and weather
